failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Agent kept a type word the clue already supplied ('Roanoke Island' for 'this island', 'Adirondack Mountains' for 'these mountains'). Another answer used the wrong number ('bear' for 'species of these', where the key is plural 'Bears'), despite existing rules on dropping head nouns and on plurals for 'these'.

rejected_edits.content:
- The CATEGORY text in an archive line is part of the puzzle. Many answers are puns or idioms tied to it (category 'WEATHER WORDS & PHRASES', clue 'W. has this type of job' -> 'high pressure'). If the archived answer looks odd as a literal reading of the clue, still trust it and copy it exactly. Do not replace it with a more literal guess from other passages.
- Aggregator and trivia pages often put the answer in the PAGE TITLE while the snippet repeats the clue verbatim: '[TLE] fall - Search-ID.com [PAR] ...a classic of this season; It follows pit, prat & rain...' -> 'Fall'; '[TLE] history - Search-ID.com [PAR] Need help in this subject... Call up Clio' -> 'History'. When a short page title sits on a snippet that contains the clue's distinctive words, treat that title word as the prime candidate and sanity-check it against the clue. Even when the snippet shows only the clue and category (e.g. 'A MUSE ME: ...'), take the anchor entity in the clue (Clio, Goneril) and answer the entity it points to using the other passages.
rejected_edits.target: Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.

rejected_edits.content:
- A clue that is just ONE proper place name ('Timonium') asks for the larger place that contains it (US state, or country for a non-US town). Passages about shops, gyms, schools, fairs or hotels there are only search hits for the name, so never answer with a topic word from them. Pick the state or country the passages attach to the place (Lutherville-Timonium, Maryland -> 'Maryland').
- Picture-reference clues ('The dipper seen here', 'shown here', 'this item pictured') come from a video or image clue you cannot see. Ignore the missing picture and answer from the textual hooks that remain: the related noun in the clue plus the passages that pair it with a single partner ('honey dipper' -> 'honey' for 'used with this sticky substance'). Do not answer with a different sense of the same word (Big Dipper, a character named Dipper).
- Parenthetical stage directions that describe a video or audio clue ('(Jon of the Clue Crew peers down between the cymbals.)') are decoration; answer from the factual part after them. A telegraphic clue with no 'this' ('Georgia guy, flag-fashioning pop painter') defines a person or thing: match EACH descriptor (birthplace, famous work, movement) against the passages and answer with the full name of the one entity that fits all of them ('Jasper Johns').
rejected_edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).

rejected_edits.content:
- Scales, measures, wars and similar named things keep their head word when the clue supplies only a generic type noun: 'this standard wind scale' -> 'Beaufort scale' (bare 'Beaufort' is incomplete); 'this 1337-1453 conflict' -> 'Hundred Years' War'. Drop only the descriptive modifiers the clue states ('standard', 'wind', '1337-1453').
- Quoted type noun: when the clue puts the generic noun itself in quotation marks after 'this' ('In 1720 bad investments in this "bubble" burst the British economy'), the quoted word is the head of a standard proper name that the passages repeat. Answer with the full name ('South Sea Bubble'), not the bare modifier ('South Sea'). This is the same head-noun exception, not an echo error.
rejected_edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).

rejected_edits.content: - Match the number the clue's pointer implies. 'species of these', 'types of these', 'these <plural noun>' or a clue where several different things share the answer ('X & Y had species of these as mascots') -> PLURAL ('Bears', not 'bear'). 'this <noun>', 'one of these' or a single described item -> singular. When the clue says 'seen here' (an image we cannot see), answer with the generic singular noun for the item that the passages tie to the clue's exact action or detail ('Hostess Cupcakes ... split in half' -> 'cupcake'), not simply the brand item mentioned most often.
rejected_edits.target: - Use the singular form for a generic single object ('Well', not 'wells'), but keep the plural for crops, commodities and mass categories ('Bananas') or when the clue says 'these'/'ones'.
